title: Return of Tensions in the South China Sea Was a Matter of Time
text:
Return of Tensions in the South China Sea Was a Matter of Time

Channel News Asia

Ezra Acayan/Getty Images

The following excerpt is from an op-ed published in Channel News Asia on September 24, 2026, written by Andrew Chubb, a Fellow on Foreign Policy and National Security at ASPI's Center for China Analysis.Tensions are once again on the rise in Asia’s most contentious waterway, after a period of relative quiet in the South China Sea.Clashes on the water have become sharper and more frequent since July. The most serious confrontation was on Jul 20, when Chinese Coast Guard personnel and Philippine marines fought with batons and paddles near Second Thomas Shoal, with a Filipino marine receiving a serious blow to the head. Most recently on Friday (Sep 18), Chinese and Philippine vessels collided near Sabina Shoal. The return of such regular clashes was all but inevitable. Read the full op-ed here.
